items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: I knew it was this guy -- what was his name? Jack Hylton. It was his band.

ctx.x: No, similar. Not note for note. Similar. Because they always kept the same -- and a lot of the times we'd make a record and a lot of times when they'd come to the solo it would even be better than on the record. And Duke would say, why didn't you put that on the record? "I never thought of it." That's right. Ain't never thought of it.

When you're speaking of white musicians, when we first went to Europe in '33, I was riding in a cab. And heard them play one of our numbers and it sounded exactly like our band until it got to the solo. Individual solos, then I knew it was this guy -- what was his name? Jack Hylton. It was his band. And he had the band, he was a Paul Whiteman of Europe. I said, oh, no, that ain't our band. I spotted it right away.
